title: The Interim That Outlived Its Deadline
blurb: Oslo set a five-year interim period that ended on 4 May 1999. Follow the attempts to reset the clock, and what became of each.

steps.teaser: The five-year interim arrangement, and the A/B/C map it created.
The first Likud-era implementation of a further-redeployment commitment.
A numbered land-transfer schedule, then a Knesset vote to stop delivering it.
A fresh timetable for the same commitments, with new deadlines.
The summit called to shortcut the missed deadlines, and the dispute over what it offered.
The most detailed American proposal, and a negotiation that said it had never been closer.
When the Palestinian leadership declared the framework over, and what kept running anyway.

title: Never Adopted, Widely Followed
blurb: Documents no government formally adopted, and the policies that ran on them anyway.

steps.teaser: A 1967 plan that was never adopted and guided settlement siting for about a decade.
A committee that found no 'occupation', and the Attorney General's check on it.
The law that carried the report's logic into statute, until the Supreme Court struck it down.
The unauthorised settlement points all of this is about.
The 1967 plan's territory, returning as a sovereignty bill.

title: Digging in Contested Ground
blurb: How archaeology in East Jerusalem became part of the argument over who holds the land.

steps.teaser: The first major excavation after Israel captured East Jerusalem.
Captured, enlarged, annexed: the ground being dug.
Where a City of David site, a settler organisation and eviction orders share one neighbourhood.
A 2005 'palace of David' claim, and the critics' reply.
A bill that would put West Bank antiquities under Israeli civilian administration.

title: From Suez to the Sinai Treaty
blurb: Three wars and one treaty over the same peninsula.

steps.teaser: A secret pact, a quick conquest, and withdrawal under American pressure.
The crisis that undid the 1957 arrangement, and the war that followed.
'From territories', not 'from the territories': a long dispute over one missing word.
A canal crossing, a ceasefire, and a shuttle.
Two frameworks: one implemented, one never.
The largest single reversal of post-1967 territorial control.
